content:
The simplest way to move your Thunderbird data from the old to the new PC would have been to transfer (copy & paste) the entire folder Thunderbird from ... \users\username\AppData\Roaming\Thunderbird\ on the old PC to the same location on the new PC as it is described in this help article https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/moving-thunderbird-data-to-a-new-computer

In your Thunderbird installation on the old PC your accounts are set up as POP accounts, but in the Thunderbird installation on the new PC you used the IMAP protocol for your accounts. That means that you can download only those incoming messages still remaining on the server and that you would probably need a tool to import all mail files from the old Thunderbird profile to Local Folders in the Thunderbird profile on the new PC.

If Thunderbird is still running on your old PC I advise to move your actual "Thunderbird" folder on the new PC to another place such as the Desktop and replace it with the "Thunderbird" folder from the old PC. The application Thunderbird must be closed when you execute this procedure.

If you want to keep your actual Thunderbird installation but have access to your old received, sent, archived.... etc messages, addresses, calendar events.... you would have to import all your mail files as well as address book and calendar files separately from the old to the new PC. This method would be more difficult and more time consuming...

content:
Hi Rose,

First, you'll want to make a back-up copy of your data and store it on an external drive. It's best to back-up your whole hard drive occasionally. Maybe you are doing this already. For now, you could also just make a copy of your Thunderbird profile. To find your profile folder, click on the Help menu > Troubleshooting information > look for "Profile Folder" in the left column of the Application Basic table, and click on "Show in [...]" next to it.

(You could export your messages from Thunderbird, which is easier than copying your profile folder, but, if you have so many messages that you have reached the limit on the server, you may also have too many messages to export.)

Now, your question.

If your account is an IMAP account and your messages are in IMAP folders, whatever you do in Thunderbird or on the server will be reflected in the other location. Deleting messages in one place will delete them everywhere. If it's easier to delete them in Thunderbird than on the server, you can do that and never deal with webmail.

But before that, you have to preserve your messages in Thunderbird. You do that by creating local folders and copying the messages to the local folders.

If your account is a POP account, messages are not sychronized, so deleting them at the server will not delete them from Thunderbird.

If you do not know your account type, click on the name of the account in the folder pane. Select "Settings" from the drop-down menu. Click on "Server Settings" on the left, and look at the top right for server type.

If you need guidance with any step, please ask.

You should not experience duplication with other folders, although Gmail may place a copy in the Important folder. My recommendation is to unsubscribe from Important and from Allmail.
